ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure shows an emitter follower circuit. The collector is connected to +12 V; the base node is labeled U1, the base is connected to +12 V through a 10 kΩ resistor, and the input terminal is coupled to U1 through C1; below the emitter two 1 kΩ resistors are connected in series to ground, and the middle node is labeled U2; the output side is coupled through C2 to the 2 kΩ load on the right, so during DC analysis C1 and C2 are both open-circuited. Then reason: In the DC equivalent circuit, C1 and C2 are open-circuited, and the right-side 2 kΩ load does not participate in the DC bias. Let the base current be IB, then the emitter current IE=(β+1)IB=101IB. The DC bias loop is: +12 V → 10 kΩ base resistor → base-emitter junction U_BEQ=0.6 V → two series 1 kΩ emitter resistors → ground. Therefore write the equation: 12 = 10 kΩ·IB + 0.6 + 2 kΩ·IE = 10 kΩ·IB + 0.6 + 2 kΩ·101IB. Solving gives IB = (12-0.6)/(10 kΩ+202 kΩ) ≈ 53.8 μA, IE≈5.43 mA. From the figure it can be seen that U2 is located at the lower end of the upper 1 kΩ emitter resistor, so U1-U2 equals the base-emitter junction voltage drop plus the DC voltage drop on the upper 1 kΩ resistor: U1-U2 = 0.6 + IE·1 kΩ ≈ 0.6 + 5.43 = 6.03 V, approximately taken as about 6.1 V according to the problem.

method.method_draft: Reduce the circuit to its DC bias network. Let UE be the emitter voltage above the two series 1 kΩ resistors. Since the two emitter resistors are equal and U2 is their midpoint, U2=UE/2. The base voltage is U1=UE+0.6. The emitter current is IE=UE/(2 kΩ), so the base current is IB=IE/(β+1). The 10 kΩ resistor from +12 V supplies this base current, so set (12-(UE+0.6))/10 kΩ = [UE/(2 kΩ)]/(β+1). Solve for UE, then compute U1-U2=(UE+0.6)-UE/2. Substituting β=100 gives approximately the standard result 6.1 V.
